reproductions.verdict: ✅ 能：官方评测脚本 + Zenodo 免注册数据 `00.zip`，出论文里那张方法对比表。

checks.name: ground_truth_is_a_binary_label_set
checks.detail: 17266247 static + 95983 dynamic + 0 other over 17362230 points

checks.name: sequence_is_the_published_one
checks.detail: 141 frames, 17362230 GT points

checks.name: the_two_eval_implementations_agree
checks.detail: official PCL binary vs independent scipy rewrite label 3000000 sampled GT points with 0 disagreements

checks.name: the_density_control_rises_with_observability
checks.detail: the naive map voxelised to 0.2 m - which deletes no structure on purpose - goes from 61.6% dropped at never-seen points to 81.5% at always-seen points. That rise is the density confound this stage exists to subtract, and if it ever reverses, the stratification is measuring something else.

checks.name: observability_strata_cover_every_bin
checks.detail: 11 maps x 6 bins, 141 frame poses

findings.name: ranking_depends_on_the_metric
findings.detail: by SA: Removert > DUFOMap > BeautyMap > ERASOR; by AA: DUFOMap > BeautyMap > ERASOR > Removert. The two orders disagree, so any single-metric ranking of these methods is a statement about the metric as much as the method.

findings.name: dynamic_points_are_a_rounding_error_of_the_map
findings.detail: 95983 of 17362230 GT points are dynamic (0.5528%). A method that deletes nothing scores ~100% SA, which is why SA alone cannot rank these methods.

findings.name: the_benchmark_row_and_the_official_row_are_not_the_same_measurement
findings.detail: On this same KITTI 00 GT, the benchmark's ROS-free port of Removert scores SA 99.44 / AA 64.26, while the authors' own repo scores SA 99.62 / AA 94.29 (official scan-side output; see 01-04). Both are recorded above under separate metric names. ERASOR's port, by contrast, is faithful in its own metric - so 'the port stands in for the method' has to be checked per method, not assumed.

findings.name: h1_prime_part3_holds_for_maps_that_actually_keep_their_points
findings.detail: Removert's official map drops only 0.38% of static GT points overall, so its dropped labels are genuine misclassification rather than downsampling: 11.7% at points no frame could see against 0.2% at points every frame could see - a 51x concentration in the low-observability stratum. The task book's H1' part 3 is therefore supported where it is testable.

findings.name: h1_prime_part3_fails_where_sa_loss_is_downsampling
findings.detail: ERASOR's map, as submitted, drops 33.3% of static points and its rate RISES with observability (14.2% never-seen -> 34.1% always-seen) - the signature of voxel downsampling (dense, well-observed surfaces lose more points to the grid), not of misclassification. For such maps 'false positive' is not a meaningful phrase until the metric is resolution-corrected.

findings.name: the_0p2m_strata_are_a_density_measurement
findings.detail: once every map is voxelised to 0.2 m, all of them - control included - sit on one rising curve (about 62% dropped at never-seen points, 82% at always-seen ones), and the method differences are a roughly constant offset. Anything measured on such maps is mostly a statement about resolution.

reproductions.note: benchmark infrastructure verified: 141 frames, 4/4 methods scored, eval cross-check 0 disagreements; false removals stratified by observability: 50.8x at never-seen vs always-seen points

checks.name: downstream_registration_was_measured_for_every_map
checks.detail: 6 maps x 141 frames at level L2; failure rate is the share of queries that did not land within (0.20 m, 2.0 deg) with inlier ratio >= 0.30

checks.name: map_quality_is_measured_on_the_registered_point_set
checks.detail: SA/DA/AA in this stage come from re-scoring the *normalised* maps the registration actually used, not from the as-submitted tables - so the comparison is between two views of one identical point set

findings.name: per_sequence_agreement_with_the_authors_own_notebook
findings.detail: the authors publish the executed notebook, so the comparison is per sequence: the largest difference is 0.157 pp on sequence 01, and every other sequence is within 0.05 pp. Ten of the eleven differences are positive and tiny while ATE is far better than theirs (1.85 m vs 7.40 m) - the signature of the deskewing fix landed in v1.2.0/v1.2.2 after the paper, not of a wrong pipeline.

findings.name: official_kitti_00_10_instead_of_a_proxy_sequence
findings.detail: the earlier run used 141 reconstructed frames of KITTI 00, which yield only 2 KITTI-devkit error samples and cannot be compared with the paper. This run is the authors' eval/kitti.ipynb setup on the official sequences.

findings.name: h1_prime_ranking_comparison
findings.detail: at the most discriminating perturbation level (L2), ranking by AA gives dufomap > beautymap > removert_port > removert_official > uncleaned > erasor_port, while ranking by registration failure gives removert_port < dufomap < removert_official < beautymap < uncleaned < erasor_port. Spearman rho(AA, localization utility) = 0.7827 at that level (utility = 100 - failure rate, so positive means the rankings agree), L0: 0.6547, L1: 0.6547, L2: 0.7827, L3: 0.5508; against the *as-submitted* SA/DA/AA the same comparison gives 0.3769 (SA: 0.2319). The task book's H1' predicts rho < 0.9, i.e. that the two rankings differ - it holds even against the kindest pairing. Spread per level: L0: spread 19.9 pp, L1: spread 19.1 pp, L2: spread 17.7 pp, L3: spread 14.2 pp.

findings.name: downstream_numbers_are_self_registration_not_a_revisit
findings.detail: the maps were built from these same 141 frames, so every query's own points are in the map it is registered into. The absolute failure rates are therefore optimistic; what the experiment supports is the *ranking* comparison, because every map is treated identically. A true revisit test needs a second session over the same place.

findings.name: the_official_erasor_map_cannot_enter_this_experiment
findings.detail: the official ERASOR output is expressed in the official bag's SuMa frame, which differs from the benchmark's world frame by ~1.6 m median nearest-neighbour distance (measured in 03_erasor). It fails 100 % of registrations at every perturbation level for that reason, so it is excluded rather than silently scored as a bad map.

findings.name: no_loop_closure_by_design
findings.detail: there is no loop closure, no pose graph and no keyframe selection. Drift is bounded only by ICP itself, which matters for the H1' experiment: a 'cleaned map hurts localization' result could be drift rather than map quality.

reproductions.note: official KITTI 00-10: mean relative translational error 0.53 % (paper 0.50 %), 23201 frames; downstream localizability rho(normalised AA, utility) = 0.7827 at level L2

checks.name: evaluator_implementations_agree
checks.detail: official export_eval_pcd vs scipy re-implementation: 0 disagreeing GT labels (rate 0.0)

findings.name: official_removert_is_not_the_conservative_extreme
findings.detail: same 141 frames, same evaluator, same GT: official Removert scores SA 99.62 / DA 89.25 / AA 94.29, the benchmark's port scores SA 99.44 / DA 41.53 / AA 64.26. The two upstream outputs of one run sit at opposite corners of the precision/recall trade-off, so 'Removert's score' is not defined without saying which output is submitted.

reproductions.title: DUFOMap: Efficient Dynamic Awareness Mapping
reproductions.static_status: 🟢 **已复现：与论文 2 位小数完全一致**
reproductions.heading: 01-05 · DUFOMap
reproductions.verdict: ✅ 能，而且最简单：`pip install dufomap` + KITTI 00 免注册数据，官方评测脚本直接出论文表 I。

checks.name: reproduces_paper_headline
checks.detail: d_p=1 gives SA/DA/AA = 97.96/98.72/98.34 vs paper 97.96/98.72/98.34 (Table I p.5), within 0.5 pp

checks.name: gt_is_binary_and_rare_dynamic
checks.detail: GT = 17266247 static + 95983 dynamic points (0.55% dynamic) - a rare-positive problem, so AA is dominated by SA

checks.name: dp_is_load_bearing
checks.detail: d_p=2 keeps +1.92 pp more static and removes -2.09 pp fewer dynamic points than the paper's d_p=1

findings.name: upstream_example_contradicts_the_paper
findings.detail: DynamicMap_Benchmark's methods/dufomap/main.py passes d_p=2 with the comment 'same with paper', but the DUFOMap paper's default - the one whose Table I row we reproduce - is d_p=1 (Table IV, p.7). Using the example's value reproduces AA only by coincidence; SA and DA are each off by about 2 pp.

findings.name: geometric_mean_hides_the_sa_da_tradeoff
findings.detail: d_p=1 -> SA 97.96 / DA 98.72 / AA 98.34; d_p=2 -> SA 99.89 / DA 96.63 / AA 98.25. The two AA values are 0.09 pp apart while SA and DA each move ~2 pp in opposite directions - the geometric mean of a rare-positive problem is almost entirely SA, so it cannot tell a conservative cleaner from an aggressive one.

findings.name: dynamic_points_are_0_55_percent_of_the_map
findings.detail: 95983 of 17362230 GT points are dynamic; any metric averaged over points is therefore a static-preservation metric in disguise.

reproductions.note: DUFOMap on KITTI 00: SA/DA/AA = 97.96/98.72/98.34 vs paper 97.96/98.72/98.34

reproductions.title: BeautyMap: Binary-Encoded Adaptable Ground Matrix for Dynamic Points Removal in Global Maps
reproductions.heading: 01-06 · BeautyMap
reproductions.verdict: ✅ 能：官方仓库 `python main.py`，配同一套官方评测，命中论文表 I。

checks.name: reproduces_paper_row
checks.detail: SA/DA/HA = 96.95/98.34/97.64 vs BeautyMap Table I p.6 96.76/98.38/97.56, within 0.5 pp

checks.name: aa_and_ha_agree_only_because_sa_da_are_close
checks.detail: AA 97.6431 vs HA 97.6407 - the two means differ by 0.0024 pp here because SA and DA are within 1.4 pp of each other. That is a property of this method on this sequence, not of the metrics.

findings.name: upstream_does_not_run_on_numpy_2
findings.detail: BeautyMap's vendored utils/pcdpy3.py calls np.fromstring (line 150) and ndarray.tostring (line 265), both removed in NumPy 2. Two LOCAL PATCHed lines (frombuffer(...).copy() and tobytes(order='C')) are required. The first failure is at read time; the second only after ~50 s of processing, at write time - a fresh clone that patches only the first looks fine until it has done all the work.

findings.name: matches_the_benchmark_papers_HA_column_too
findings.detail: This run also reproduces the HA column that the BeautyMap paper prints for the other methods: Removert 41.53/58.59 and ERASOR 98.54/79.55 predicted from this paper's Table I, and measured here as 41.5313/58.591 and 98.5352/79.5563. Two papers and four methods now agree on the same numbers, which is the strongest evidence we have that the whole data-and-evaluation chain is right.

findings.name: beautymap_is_the_balanced_one
findings.detail: BeautyMap SA 96.95 / DA 98.34 sits between Removert's refuse-to-delete (99.44/41.53) and ERASOR's delete-too-much (66.71/98.54), and is the only one of the four with both above 96.

reproductions.note: BeautyMap on KITTI 00: SA/DA/HA = 96.95/98.34/97.64 vs paper 96.76/98.38/97.56

reproductions.title: DynoSAM: Open-Source Smoothing and Mapping Framework for Dynamic SLAM
reproductions.static_status: ⛔ **本机不可跑**：上游在 `cmake` configure 阶段就要求 CUDA 工具链（`nvcc`/TensorRT/`cudaoptflow.hpp`），与数据无关 —— 见 [`work/feasibility.md`](work/feasibility.md)
reproductions.heading: 01-07 · DynoSAM
reproductions.verdict: 🟡 **原来的判读要改**：CUDA 不是死结 —— `nvcc` 可以**在没有 GPU 的机器上安装**（已实测：conda-forge `cuda-nvcc` 装上 CUDA 13.4 编译器），`-DDYNOSAM_NN_USE_TRT=OFF` 又能去掉 TensorRT，两者一起就把 configure 阶段的 CUDA 门去掉了。真正剩下的是**一整套 ROS 2 + GTSAM 工作区**（上游对着 ROS 2 Kilted 写，本机是 Jazzy）。
reproductions.note: GPU/CUDA absent, and DynoSAM cannot even `cmake`-configure without it: dynosam_nn/CMakeLists.txt:3 declares `LANGUAGES C CXX CUDA`, :105 compiles a .cu source, :128-129 link TensorRT + cudart unconditionally, and FeatureTracker.hpp:33 includes <opencv2/cudaoptflow.hpp> with no guard (nvcc/NvInfer.h/CUDA OpenCV are all absent here). Runtime flags cannot help - the no-TensorRT path is already the default. Evidence: work/feasibility.md. Needs a CUDA GPU, not data or code changes.

checks.name: reproduces_paper_ate
checks.detail: ATE (rigid, no scale) = 0.0157 m vs paper 0.015 m (Table I p.5, f3/walking_xyz), within 0.003

checks.name: reproduces_paper_rpe_translation
checks.detail: RPE translation = 0.0201 m/s vs paper 0.02 m/s, within 0.003

checks.name: every_frame_was_processed
checks.detail: 827 poses written; the paper requires processing all 827 frames, and both mechanisms (mask propagation and optical flow) depend on frame-to-frame continuity

findings.name: rotational_rpe_depends_on_an_unspecified_convention
findings.detail: our rotational RPE is 0.604 °/s by RMSE but 0.475 °/s by mean, against the paper's 0.47 °/s. The column is headed only 'RPE rotation (°/s)'. The distribution is skewed (median far below the max), which is exactly when the choice matters. Translation shows the same asymmetry but much smaller, so it happens to agree either way.

findings.name: cheap_semantics_is_the_actual_contribution
findings.detail: reading the official source, the system DOES use a neural network (YOLO-fastest-xl at 320x320, System.cc:217) - what it removes is the tracker's dependency on waiting for it (Tracking.cc:1592 never blocks, Tracking.cc:4286 propagates the old mask with LK optical flow). So it is a scheduling result, not a geometry-only result, and it inherits COCO's blind spot for unknown dynamic objects.

findings.name: wall_clock_is_the_same_order_as_the_paper
findings.detail: mean tracking 20.76 ms/frame vs the paper's 16.72 ms (~60 FPS). Measured headless on different hardware, so this supports 'same order of magnitude on CPU', not an exact match.

reproductions.note: NGD-SLAM on TUM fr3/walking_xyz: ATE 0.0157 m vs paper 0.015 m; RPE trans 0.0201 m/s vs 0.02

checks.name: evaluator_implementations_agree
checks.detail: official export_eval_pcd vs scipy re-implementation: 0 disagreeing GT labels (rate 0.0)

checks.name: official_run_reached_the_end_of_its_pipeline
checks.detail: saveAllTypeOfScans() - the last statement of Removerter::run() - wrote 81 files per directory into scans_nd_strong/ (81), scans_updated/ (81), scans_updated_strong/ (81); the output directory is wiped before the run and the driver removes the completion marker first, so these cannot be a previous run's leftovers

checks.name: change_detection_found_both_directions
checks.detail: nd_map.pcd (central-only) 218931 points, pd_map.pcd (query-only) 43853 points; both empty would mean the two sessions saw identical geometry and nothing was measured

findings.name: coverage_caps_the_comparable_score
findings.detail: only 71.6% of the benchmark's GT static points (12363618 of 17266247) are observed by the 110 input scans this run consumed (92.2% for dynamic). On the full 141-frame GT the same map scores SA 49.51 / DA 76.50, i.e. the sibling rows (removert 99.44 / erasor 66.71 / dufomap 97.96 SA) are not like-for-like: their maps cover all 141 frames. The coverage-matched GT (SA 69.14 / DA 74.51) is the fair partner.

findings.name: the_sa_loss_is_a_deliberate_trade_for_dynamic_rejection
findings.detail: on one identical GT - the central session's own footprint, 11497294 static / 49658 dynamic points, against which all three maps are measured - the no-removal control (the raw central map, 2675552 points) scores SA 99.44 / DA 1.65: it keeps everything and rejects nothing. After the change detection, updated_map.pcd scores SA 69.75 / DA 79.22 and the merged scan-side output SA 64.08 / DA 79.85. So the detector trades 29.7 pp of static preservation for 77.6 pp of dynamic rejection on this pair - aggressive next to 01-04's Removert run on the same kind of data (SA 99.62 / DA 89.25), which is upstream's own configuration difference: 01-04 runs params_kitti.yaml with dist_nn_points_within 0.1, ltremovert's params_ltmapper.yaml asks for 0.01, i.e. a ten times stricter requirement that two sessions agree.

findings.name: the_run_has_two_upstream_outputs_and_they_are_close
findings.detail: on the identical central-session GT, map-side updated_map.pcd scores SA 69.75 / DA 79.22 (758034 points) and the scan-side merged scans_updated/ SA 64.08 / DA 79.85 (7100330 points) - AA 74.33 vs 71.53. Unlike 01-04, where the two outputs of one Removert run sat at opposite corners of the trade-off, here the choice of output moves AA by 2.8 pp; what moves this score is which GT footprint it is measured on (central GT AA 74.33, both-sessions GT AA 71.78, full 141-frame GT AA 61.54).

findings.name: nd_pd_asymmetry_is_the_signature_of_a_partial_overlap
findings.detail: central-only points (nd_map) 218931 vs query-only points (pd_map) 43853 - a 5.0x asymmetry. The query session covers a ~15 m stretch of the central session's 40.8 m trajectory, so far more of the central map is unseen by the query than the other way round. A real multi-session pair (the paper's two visits to one car park) would not have this shape.

findings.name: the_paper_headline_is_not_reachable_from_this_checkout
findings.detail: LT-mapper's delta-map numbers (85.7 MB vs 213.6 MB, 9.8 s vs 87/160 s) belong to the LT-map module, which is absent from the repository: a whole-checkout grep for delta_map/meta_map returns nothing and Removerter.cpp:1671 mentions it only in a comment. Tab. I/II also need MulRan KAIST 04, an extended sequence obtained by e-mail. No run of this checkout can produce those numbers, in any environment.

findings.name: what_change_means_on_this_input
findings.detail: one continuous KITTI 00 pass split at frames 4390..4470 / 4451..4530, not the paper's six sessions over three days. 'Change' here is moving cars plus occlusion and viewpoint differences between two nearby stretches of one drive; the gap between these numbers and the paper's ParkingLot experiment is the experiment, not the implementation.

findings.name: runtime
findings.detail: the official node ran over 81 central + 29 query keyframes in 36 s wall clock (it does all the work in its constructor and then spins; the same input took ~32 s on a cold page cache and ~8 s warm, so read this as seconds, not as a benchmark). This is not the paper's 9.8 s figure: that one times the LT-map delta-map update, whose code is absent here, and it is not comparable to a whole change-detection pass.

findings.name: roi_rule_recomputed_from_the_poses_matches_the_run
findings.detail: work/make_coverage_matched_gt.py recomputes Session.cpp:234's 10 m ROI rule from the two pose files and gets 29 query keyframes, the same number ltremovert logged - so the fair GT's footprint really is the run's input footprint.

reproductions.note: official ltremovert on a two-session KITTI 00 split (81 central + 29 query keyframes): SA/DA/AA = 69.14/74.51/71.78 on the coverage-matched GT (71.6% of GT static observable), 49.51/76.50 on the full 141-frame GT; LT-map/delta-map half of the paper is absent from the repo

findings.name: the_multi_session_step_needs_a_manual_icp_guess

findings.name: the_dataset_itself_was_quota_limited
findings.detail: ParkingLot comes from Google Drive with a per-file download quota: plain downloads return a 2009-byte 'Quota exceeded' page, while 1 MB ranged requests keep working (observed: fine up to ~224 MB, then nothing). reproductions/tools/gdrive_range_fetch.py pulls both zips in ranged chunks which is why this folder has data at all.

findings.name: open3d_0_18_needs_numpy_1_x_and_two_source_patches
findings.detail: recorded in work/local_patches.patch: (1) map_zipper.py imports the optional pygicp matcher unconditionally, but that matcher is not on PyPI (needs fast_gicp built from source) - wrapped in try/except, and the config uses Open3DScanMatcher anyway; (2) per-frame `combined += pcd` accumulation segfaults on Open3D 0.18 - replaced by one np.vstack, same points, no algorithm change. Neither patch touches the ephemerality logic that the paper is about.

findings.name: the_choice_of_second_cloud_moves_the_metric
findings.detail: measuring session 01 against session 02's own cleaned map gives AC 0.971 / RMSE 0.068 / CD 0.090, and against the merged lifelong map 0.999 / 0.083 / 0.138. The paper does not specify which one Table I uses, so both are recorded rather than one being presented as 'the' number.
